title: Generics
description: Write reusable, type-safe functions and structures that work across types without sacrificing type information.

challenges.title: What do generics solve?
challenges.description:
Why would you use a generic instead of `any`?

  A)  Generics are faster at runtime
  B)  Generics preserve type information — the return type relates to the input type
  C)  Generics allow any value just like any does, but look nicer
  D)  Generics only work with arrays
challenges.whyMatters: Generic utility functions — wrappers, parsers, result types — are how production tooling stays typed end-to-end without casting everything to any.
hints: Think about what you lose when you return any from a function

choices.label: A)  Generics are faster at runtime
B)  Generics preserve type information — the return type relates to the input type
C)  Generics allow any value just like any does, but look nicer
D)  Generics only work with arrays

challenges.title: Read generic syntax
challenges.whyMatters: You'll call generic functions constantly — understanding what T resolves to tells you what type you're working with downstream.
hints: TypeScript infers T from the argument you pass in

challenges.title: Generic constraints
challenges.whyMatters: Constrained generics let you write functions that work on arrays, strings, and custom collections — all things that have length — without losing type safety.
hints: extends in a constraint means 'must be assignable to'

choices.label: A)  T must be a subclass of { length: number }
B)  T can be anything but defaults to { length: number }
C)  T must have at least a `length: number` property
D)  T is replaced by { length: number } at compile time

challenges.title: Write a generic identity function
challenges.whyMatters: Wrapper types appear everywhere in production tooling — Result<T>, ApiResponse<T>, CacheEntry<T>. This is the simplest version of that pattern.
hints: Declare a type parameter: function wrap<T>(value: T)
The return type can be written as { value: T }

challenges.title: Generic interface
challenges.whyMatters: Typed API response wrappers are the first thing you write when building any HTTP client or service integration.
hints: Substitute T with User[] everywhere T appears

challenges.title: Write a typed Result type
challenges.description:
Define a generic `Result<T>` type that represents either success or failure:

- On success: `{ ok: true, value: T }`
- On failure: `{ ok: false, error: string }`

Then write two helper functions:
- `succeed<T>(value: T): Result<T>` — creates a success result
- `fail<T>(error: string): Result<T>` — creates a failure result

And a function `unwrap<T>(result: Result<T>): T` that returns the value or throws the error string.
challenges.whyMatters: The Result pattern replaces throw/catch in functional production code — config parsers, health checkers, and CLI tools all benefit from explicit error handling without exceptions.
hints: Use a union type for Result<T>: success shape | failure shape
In unwrap, narrow with result.ok to access result.value safely
throw result.error works since error is a string

challenges.title: Generic with keyof constraint
challenges.whyMatters: Extracting a single field from an array of service objects, log entries, or config records is a very common scripting pattern.
hints: K extends keyof T ensures the key actually exists on T
T[K] is the type of the value at key K on object T
